name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: The Bulgarian split squat is a unilateral lower body exercise in which the rear foot is elevated on a bench while the front foot bears most of the load. It provides deep quadriceps and glute stimulation with a significant hip flexor stretch on the rear leg. It is considered one of the most challenging and effective single-leg movements for hypertrophy.

execution.starting_position: Stand about two feet in front of a bench. Place the top of the rear foot on the bench. Front foot should be far enough forward that the shin remains near-vertical at the bottom of the movement.
execution.setup_instructions: Test the front foot position before adding load. If the front knee tracks excessively over the toes, step the front foot further forward.
steps: Lower the body by bending the front knee, keeping the torso upright.
Descend until the rear knee is just above the floor.
Drive through the front heel to return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on the drive up.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench — causes excessive forward knee travel
Knee caving inward on the front leg
safety_considerations: If balance is an issue, hold onto a fixed surface with one hand initially
Hip flexor on the rear leg will be stretched aggressively — ease into depth
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee nearly touching the floor at the bottom. Full extension of front leg at top.
coaching_cues: Drop straight down — do not lean forward
Front shin stays close to vertical throughout the descent
